message.content:
Build a NEW marketing homepage concept for Nxeon at route `/newwebsitev5`. This is one of four concepts being built in parallel for a bake-off; yours must be visually unmistakable from the others.

## Your concept: v5 — "Instrument". Dark, technical, Swiss.

Near-black ground. Monospace-led. Hairline rules. Dense, real data laid out like a spec sheet or a measurement instrument — think an oscilloscope readout, a Bloomberg terminal, a Braun product manual. **No photography and no illustration at all.** Type, rules, numbers and one signal colour carry the entire page.

The audience is developers who distrust marketing pages. Every claim should be checkable. Restraint is the point — this concept wins by looking like it was made by engineers, not by a marketing team.

- Layout: a visible grid. Let the column structure show. Wide tables of real plan data are welcome where other concepts would use cards.
- Type: pick a real monospace as a *display* face (not just for data) paired with one neutral sans. Do NOT use Inter, Geist, or Space Grotesk — all three read as generated-page defaults. Load via `next/font/google`.
- One accent colour only, reserved for interactive elements. Everything else greyscale/near-black.
- Interaction: something genuinely useful and tactile — e.g. an interactive plan comparator driven by real Plan/GamePlan rows, keyboard-navigable. Not decorative.

## Repo context

- Root: `/opt/nxeon`. Next.js App Router, Tailwind v4, TypeScript. **Work directly in /opt/nxeon.**
- Create `app/newwebsitev5/layout.tsx`, `app/newwebsitev5/page.tsx`, `app/newwebsitev5/v5.css`, plus any client components in that directory. **Touch no files outside `app/newwebsitev5/`** — three other agents are working in this same checkout in parallel.
- The layout must wrap children in `<div className="v5 ...">` and scope ALL your CSS under `.v5` so it cannot leak. Import your css from the layout.
- Set `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` in the layout's `metadata`.
- The ROOT layout already imports `globals.css` (Tailwind) and loads Geist as `--font-nx-sans` / `--font-nx-mono`. Tailwind utilities are available.
- Page should be a Server Component (`export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`) that queries real data and passes it to client components for interactivity.

## Real data sources (use these — do not hardcode numbers)

- `db.plan` — VPS plans (`priceCents`, `active`). Cheapest active ~$8.99.
- `db.gamePlan` — game plans: `gameFamily`, `ramMB`, `cpuCores`, `diskGB`, `slots`, `priceCents`, `active`. 42 active families.
- `db.gameMod.count({ where: { active: true, upstreamOk: true } })` — mod catalogue size.
- `db.osTemplate` — real one-click templates/OS images (`name`, `active`): Docker, Node.js, WordPress, Nextcloud, Gitea, Jellyfin, Ubuntu, Debian, AlmaLinux, etc.
- Regions: `import { regionsFrom } from "@/lib/nx/catalog"` with `db.node.findMany({ where: { enabled: true }, select: { id: true, region: true } })`. Returns exactly TWO: `sgp1` (Singapore) and `fsn1` (Germany). `CUSTOMER_REGION_LABELS` from `@/lib/node-regions` gives customer-facing names.
- Game metadata: `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG`, `GAME_GENRES` from `@/lib/games`; `GAME_URL_SLUG` from `@/lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings`.
- `db` is `import { db } from "@/lib/db"`.

## HONESTY CONSTRAINTS — hard requirements

- **No testimonials, reviews, or ratings.** The `Review` and `Testimonial` tables are empty. Do not invent any, no Google/Trustpilot widgets.
- **No invented statistics.** No customer counts, no "5+ data centres", no continents count. Nxeon has exactly TWO regions.
- **No partner or customer logos** implying a relationship. Real one-click templates are fine (a customer can actually deploy them). Third-party tool logos must be framed "works with", no affiliation implied.
- Two claims ARE pre-approved by the owner: `99.99% network` and the tagline `online in 47 seconds`.
- Prices must come from the database, not string literals.

## Known traps in this codebase

- **Do NOT export an object-of-components from a `"use client"` module and read properties off it in a Server Component.** e.g. `export const Icon = { arrow: () => <svg/> }` in a client file, then `<Icon.arrow/>` in the server page → resolves to `undefined` and React throws "Element type is invalid". Put shared SVG icons in a module with NO `"use client"` directive.
- A CSS rule like `.v5 .card { position: relative }` has specificity (0,2,0) and **beats** Tailwind's `lg:absolute` (0,1,0). If a Tailwind positioning utility must win, put it on a wrapper element.
- `public/logos/caddy.svg` is a 0-byte file — do not reference it.
- Grids stretch rows to the tallest sibling by default; use `content-start` / `items-start` or you'll get large dead bands.
- Keep the page readable **at rest** — never park content at `opacity: 0` waiting on a scroll observer. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Assets

- `/logo.png` (NX lockup) and `/nx-mark.png` (mark) — the real brand marks. Use these, never invent a logo.
- `/logos/*.svg` — real app/OS logos.

## Process

Two-pass design process: write a short design plan first (palette as 4-6 named hex values, 2+ typefaces with roles, layout concept in a sentence or two), then **review that plan against the concept** and revise anything that reads like a generic default you'd produce for any page, noting what you changed. Only then write code.

Build the hero plus 3-4 sections. Prefer fewer, better sections.

## Rules

- `npx tsc --noEmit` from `/opt/nxeon` must pass when you're done. Note: other agents are editing the same checkout, so if tsc reports errors in `app/newwebsitev6|v7|v8/**` those are not yours — ignore them and confirm your own files are clean.
- **Do NOT run any git command. Do NOT commit, branch, or stage anything.** Leave your files on disk; the parent session commits all four concepts together.
- **Do NOT deploy and do NOT run `npm run build`.** Concurrent builds have corrupted `.next` and taken production down before.
- Report back: what you built (file list), your design plan and what your self-review changed, and anything you could not verify.

content.thinking:
I'm confirming the real site routes to reference, avoiding the retired /docs path, and settling on ones like /developers, /pricing, /status, /compare, and /security. Now I'm starting to sketch out the design plan, beginning with a color palette.

Rather than defaulting to Nxeon's brand cyan/violet, which would feel too much like every generic dev-tool page, I'm leaning toward an amber/orange signal color on a near-black greyscale for this "instrument" concept — closer to Braun or Bloomberg terminal aesthetics — since the other bake-off concepts will likely lean on the brand navy/violet/cyan anyway, and this needs to be visually distinct.

I'm settling on `--sig: #FFB020` for interactive elements like links, focus rings, and buttons, keeping everything else greyscale — an amber-filled button with black text feels genuinely Braun/Bloomberg rather than cheap. For typography, I'm choosing Martian Mono for display, labels, and numerals, and now thinking through the body text pairing.

For layout, I'm imagining a visible 12-column grid with hairline rules running the full page height, where each section reads as a bordered "instrument block" with numbered headers (§01/§02) and right-aligned spec captions; the hero pairs a giant mono statement with a right-hand readout panel of live figures styled like a measurement display. For interaction, I'm sketching a keyboard-navigable plan comparator table covering the 4 VPS plans plus 42 game-family rows, where arrow keys move an amber cursor row and Enter triggers the deploy link, alongside a unit toggle I still need to define.

Rather than fake hourly billing, I'll build a per-resource normalization toggle ($/GB RAM, $/vCPU, $/GB disk) computed from real database values, plus a first-term/renewal price toggle since introPriceCents is genuine data — both honest, checkable features. Sectioning it out: hero with readout and CTA, then §01 the VPS plan comparator with derived cost-per-unit columns and the pricing toggle, then §02 covering game families.

Adding to the plan: §02 becomes a dense 42-row sortable table for game families linking to real landing pages, §03 indexes the 72 OS templates by category without logos, and §04 covers the two data center regions plus footer specs — giving hero plus four sections as the brief wants. Now I'm starting a self-review pass to catch anything that feels like a generic default choice, starting with the dark-plus-accent color scheme.

Since the "dark + monospace" look is itself a common dev-tool cliché, I want to make the grid rules literally visible rather than just implied — drawing real hairline column dividers as a fixed background layer using a repeating gradient across twelve columns, plus a left gutter measurement rail with section numbers and tick marks like a ruler. This turns the "instrument" concept into something structural instead of just a color choice. The second generic pattern to fix is the standard centered hero with headline, subhead, and two buttons — instead I want an asymmetric, left-aligned hero where the subhead is replaced by a specification block styled like a definition list with dotted leaders, similar to a real spec sheet.

The headline itself shouldn't read like marketing copy — it should look like a product designation line, followed by the pre-approved tagline rendered as a machine readout timestamp, which gives it an honest instrument feel. For color, I'm rethinking the amber-on-black scheme since it's both a Bloomberg cliché and can read as a warning signal — so I want to restrict amber to very small areas like focus states, hover, selection, and one filled CTA button, plus use it functionally as the cursor indicator in the comparator (a left bar and underline on the active row), keeping everything else greyscale.

Beyond that, I want the strongest concept-specific detail to be a literal provenance column: every figure in the readout should cite its actual database source in small type, directly appealing to developers skeptical of marketing pages — this feels like the most distinctive and confident choice. And visually, I'm stripping away all rounded corners, shadows, and gradients except a grid-rule background, using only 1px hairlines.

For the tables, I want genuine `<table>` markup rather than styled cards — collapsed borders, monospace tabular numerals, right-aligned numbers, uppercase header labels, and a subtle 3% hover state. The 42-row game table should support keyboard-accessible column sorting via buttons in the header cells, and everything stays static except an amber cursor transition, respecting reduced-motion preferences. I'm also weighing whether Martian Mono at small sizes with tight tracking works well for the dense table.

Since long entries like game titles won't fit well in Martian Mono, I'll switch to Public Sans for text cells and keep Martian Mono only for numerals. I'm also considering whether to include the actual brand mark PNG in the nav and footer at small size, since the guidelines call for using real brand assets rather than illustration — I want to check what it actually looks like before committing.

Writing gradient background styles...

For the left measurement rail, I'm thinking through options like rotated section numbers with tick marks, but leaning away from rotation since it feels gimmicky and considering a simpler header treatment instead.

I'm structuring each section header as a 12-column grid: number in column 1, title spanning columns 2-7, caption in 8-12, with a hairline border on top to make the grid visible. ## Design plan (pass 1)

**Palette** — `--ink #07080A` (near-black ground), `--ink-rise #0C0E11` (raised blocks), `--rule #1A1D22` (hairline), `--rule-hi #2A2F36` (emphasised hairline), `--fg #EDEFF2` / `--fg-mid #949AA3` / `--fg-dim #5C626B`, and one signal colour `--sig #FFB020` (amber).

**Type** — **Martian Mono** 300/400/500 as the *display* face (hero headline, every label, every number) + **Public Sans** 400/500 for prose only. Not Inter/Geist/Space Grotesk, and deliberately not Archivo (v1/v2) or IBM Plex (v3).

**Layout** — a literally drawn 12-column grid behind the whole sheet; hero plus four numbered sections (§01 comparator, §02 game index, §03 image catalogue, §04 footprint), each opening on a hairline with `§NN` in the first column.

## Self-review — what I changed and why

1. **"Dark + mono + one accent" is the most generic dev-tool look there is.** So the grid stopped being implied and became *painted* — a 1px line at every twelfth, and table columns pinned to `<colgroup>` twelfths under `table-layout: fixed` so boundaries land on the drawn rules. Verified: matrix boundaries sit at exactly 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 twelfths.
2. **Hero was heading → subhead → two buttons.** Replaced the subhead's job with a live spec readout, and made the headline the thesis rather than a pitch: *"Every figure on this page is a live query."*
3. **The biggest change: a provenance column.** Every figure prints the database column it came from (`Plan.introPriceCents`, `GameMod.upstreamOk`, `Node.enabled`), and §01's readout prints the actual arithmetic (`2099¢ ÷ 8 GB`). Nothing else I could have added serves "developers who distrust marketing pages" as directly.
4. **Three solid amber blocks** (CTA + two segmented switches) made the accent the loudest thing on a restraint-themed page. Pressed segments became amber ring + 12% tint; exactly one solid amber fill survives.
5. **Amber-on-black is a Bloomberg cliché**, so accent area was cut to: focus rings, hover, the grid cursor, the selected control, the best-value-per-unit markers, one CTA.
6. Zero radius, zero shadow-as-depth, zero decorative gradients. The only gradients draw the column rules and the ruler-tick strips.
7. Nothing parked at `opacity: 0`; the sheet is complete with JS off, and `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured.

## Interaction

§01 is a `role="grid"`: arrows/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown move a cursor, `1–4` jump columns, `B` toggles first-term↔renewal, `I` toggles absolute↔indexed unit rows, `Enter` opens `/dashboard/deploy?product=vps&plan=<id>`. §02 sorts by any column, filters by text or genre, `/` focuses the filter. All confirmed working against a real dev server.

## Honesty

No testimonials/reviews/ratings, no invented stats, no partner logos. Every price and count is a request-time query — which mattered: **`Plan.priceCents` changed three times while I was building** (starter went 1598 → 1278), so any literal would already be stale. §04 carries an explicit "what this sheet does not claim" block. Only `99.99% network` and `47 seconds` are stated as claims.

Two judgement calls worth flagging: I used `CUSTOMER_REGION_LABELS` and dropped `REGION_LABELS`' datacentre city and the per-region host counts, since `lib/node-regions.ts` documents that the precise city is for ops screens and it edges toward naming infrastructure. And §02 lists the **41** families that have a catalogue page, not all 42 — `ACTIVE_GAME_FAMILIES` deliberately withholds `stationeers`, so a line under the table states the 42/41 difference rather than hiding it or linking to a withheld page.

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` reports **0 errors in my files** (the one remaining error is `app/newwebsitev7/page.tsx(266): Cannot find name 'NetTable'` — another agent's in-progress file). I did not build, deploy, or run any git command. A sibling agent had a self-contained repo sandbox on port 3055 (not `/opt/nxeon/.next`), so I verified the real route end-to-end there: both fonts load via `next/font`, zero page/console errors, no horizontal overflow at 1440px or 390px, and every interaction above exercised with Playwright.

Six real bugs found and fixed by that pass, three of them specificity/order traps:
- `.v5 .foot a` (0,2,1) out-specified `.v5 .brand` (0,2,0) and broke the footer lockup into a stack — the exact trap the brief warned about, in my own CSS.
- `.cat-item span:first-child` was matching the nested version span and rendering it at 12px in primary ink instead of 9.5px dim.
- A mobile-readout rule written *after* its media query won on source order and never took effect.
- `.src { white-space: nowrap }` as a global default let one 273px provenance string push the document 19px past a 390px viewport.
- The Source column at 1/12 clipped `Plan.introPriceCents`; widened to 2/12, which also keeps every boundary on a whole twelfth.
- The price row's source label said `Plan.priceCents` even on the first-term basis.

**Not verified:** I could not test a real click-through into `/dashboard/deploy` (authed route), and the two intent deep links (`?product=vps&plan=<Plan.id>`, `?product=vps&region=<code>`) are built from `lib/deploy-intent.ts`'s documented `DEPLOY_PARAM` keys but were not exercised against the wizard.
